text: A synthesis problem set spanning chapters 4 and 5: entanglement, Bell states, the CHSH inequality, no-cloning, teleportation, and superdense coding. Every number here was already verified earlier in the course.

Problem one: build Phi-plus from ket-00 using only Hadamard and CNOT. Hadamard on qubit 1 gives ket-00 plus ket-10 over root 2; CNOT then flips qubit 2 wherever qubit 1 is 1, turning the ket-10 term into ket-11 and leaving ket-00 alone — exactly Phi-plus. Problem two: prove it's entangled. Assuming it factors requires a-c equal one over root 2, a-d equal zero, b-c equal zero, and b-d equal one over root 2. A-d equal zero forces a or d to be zero, but either choice contradicts a-c or b-d being nonzero. Contradiction — genuinely entangled.

Problem three: using angles zero, ninety, forty-five, and one-thirty-five degrees, the CHSH value comes out to 2 root 2, about 2.828, exceeding the classical bound of 2. What does this actually prove? That no local-hidden-variable theory — no model with pre-determined answers and no instantaneous influence — can reproduce these correlations. It does not prove faster-than-light signaling, and it doesn't mean anything goes — it specifically rules out the classical shared-randomness explanation, nothing more.

Problem four: Alice teleports 0.6 ket-zero plus 0.8 ket-one to Bob. Walking through all four outcomes, each with probability 0.25: Phi-plus needs no correction; Phi-minus needs a Z to flip the sign back; Psi-plus needs an X to swap the amplitudes back; Psi-minus needs X then Z. All four converge to exactly the original state once corrected, summing to a combined probability of 1 that Bob succeeds.

Problem five: why doesn't this contradict no-cloning? No-cloning forbids two copies existing at once, while the first still exists. In teleportation, Alice's Bell measurement destroys her original qubit in the very act of extracting the outcome needed to complete the protocol. At no point do Alice and Bob both hold the state — it's relocated, not duplicated. Fully consistent with no-cloning, not an exception to it.
Next lesson is the capstone: the real test of whether this course landed — explaining, clearly and accurately, every idea that actually matters, start to finish.
